en.title: Quora OA #1: Count Powers of k
en.description: Given an integer array arr and an integer k, count how many numbers in the array are powers of k, that is, numbers that can be written as k^e for a positive integer e.
en.input: The first line contains two integers n and k; the second line contains n integers arr[0..n−1]. 1≤n≤200000, 2≤k≤10^18, 2≤arr[i]≤10^18.
en.output: Output one integer: the number of elements that are powers of k.
en.explanation:
Example 1: arr=[11,121,10], k=11. 11=11^1 and 121=11^2, but 10 is not, so the answer is 2.
Example 2: 2, 4, 8, and 1024 are all powers of 2, but 6 is not, so the answer is 4.
Example 3: none of 10, 20, 30 is a power of 5, so the answer is 0.
hints: When k≥2, there are at most 60 powers of k not exceeding 10^18.
When generating powers, check whether the next one would exceed the upper bound before computing it, to avoid overflow.
Do not use floating-point logarithms for the check; the precision is not sufficient.
